biggest_catch: The $95 annual fee means your year-one net bonus math is $600 minus $95 = $505 — still strongly positive in year one, but only pursue it if you can comfortably reach $4,000 in already-planned spending within 90 days; forcing spend destroys the math.
catches: The $4,000-in-90-days threshold is high — only pursue it if you already have that much planned spending (bills, travel, everyday purchases). Never overspend or manufacture spend.
The $95 annual fee is charged from year one, so the net year-one bonus value is $600 - $95 = $505 before counting ordinary purchase rewards.
Bank of America did not state the bonus posting timing on the fetched card page — do not assume a date.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily dip your credit score by a few points.
The card's variable APR (around 20%+) will erase the entire bonus in a month or two if you carry a balance — pay the full statement balance every month.
